classes.label: Indeterminate — no usable geometry
classes.basis: the warning carries no parseable polygon or circle

classes.label: Local area enclosing the launch site
classes.basis: polygon surrounds the site rather than extending on one azimuth; consistent with an air-defence engagement zone or an initial-stage drop area, and cannot discriminate between them

classes.label: Extended corridor, no coupled impact zone
classes.basis: corridor beyond 300 km but no far-field impact zone found, so the full flight distance is unknown

classes.label: Medium-range — coupled impact zone
classes.basis: a far-field impact zone 1,000–3,500 km down-range shares this warning's window

classes.label: Strategic range — distant coupled impact zone
classes.basis: a far-field impact zone beyond 3,500 km down-range shares this warning's window

classes.label: Medium-range — self-contained corridor
classes.basis: this warning's own danger area extends 1,000–3,500 km down-range, so no second impact-zone warning is needed to establish the range class

classes.label: Strategic range — self-contained corridor
classes.basis: this warning's own danger area extends beyond 3,500 km down-range — the launch corridor and the impact fan are declared in a single polygon

response.disclaimer: Public reference data (DRDO/PIB releases, NTI, Wikipedia). `integration_sites` is context only — no site is monitored and no scoring uses it. Sentiry holds nothing about the location or movement of deployed systems; it reads published test announcements. Corridor classes narrow a candidate field and never identify a system.
